newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Duma speaker wants Yeltsin to resign if too sick.
newsitem.headline: Duma speaker wants Yeltsin to resign if too sick.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin should consider retiring if doctors rule he is unfit for heart surgery and ask him to cut down on his activity, the communist speaker of Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament said on Monday.

"I think that if the doctors give the president an exact diagnosis...how many hours he is able to work...and if they say this schedule is too restricted, so that it does not let the president work flat out, then in all probability he himself should ask to retire," Gennady Seleznyov told reporters.

Yeltsin, 65, said earlier this month he had agreed to undergo bypass surgery to improve blood supply to his heart. He said in a televised interview that the operation was likely to take place in late September.
Yeltsin said that he was given a choice of either having the operation or limiting himself to a "passive" way of life.

"When he spoke on television he told the viewers that if there were no operation his work schedule would have to be easy. And the situation in Russia is such that (the president) cannot have an easy work schedule," Seleznyov said.
But a surgeon tipped to lead the team preparing to operate on Yeltsin suggested at the weekend that the surgery might have to be postponed or even cancelled.

Renat Akchurin, appearing on NTV commercial television on Sunday, made clear that the operation could take place only if a council of doctors which was due to meet on Wednesday decided that the risks of carrying out the surgery were reasonable.

Russia's constitution says that the president should lay down his powers if he is found "persistently incapable" of carrying out his duties due to bad health. But it does not mention who can make such a decision.
